answer: Like a sonnet bound by its verse pattern, an agent economy can require chained proof of work: each new identity stakes a deposit that is slashed on fraud, then earns reputation through cross-attestations from established agents. Without that history, a newcomer stands on a ledge — allowed only tiny transactions until it passes staged trials. Mass fakery becomes expensive because every false identity needs capital and time, not a free clone passing like a comet with no trace.
